 News Flash
 November 3 Election Reminders
 News & Announcements
 Posted on October 22, 2026 
 The 2026 State Election will take place on Tuesday, November 3.  Voters will cast ballots for state and federal officials and weigh in on nine ballot questions. 
 To learn more about the ballot questions, go to the State Elections webpages.  Voters are encouraged to come prepared. Due to the complexity of the questions, most voters are taking about 15-minutes to complete ballots.  
 To avoid lines expected on Election Day, consider voting early. 
 Early Voting In-Person 
Early voting in-person continues through Friday, October 30 at Town Hall (525 Washington Street) from 8 a.m. and 4 p.m. on weekdays, and on Saturday, October 23 from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. On Thursday, October 29, Town Hall is open until 8 p.m. for evening voting. 
 Other special hours and voting locations also open to the public are:
 Tuesday, October 27 at Sisters of Charity (125 Oakland Street) from 2 p.m. to 4 p.m.
 Wednesday, October 28 at Waterstone Senior Living (27 Washington Street) from 6 p.m. to 8 p.m. 
 Voter Registration 
The last day to register to vote for the State Election is Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 5 p.m. U.S. citizens who live in Wellesley and are at least 18 years of age on election day may register at Town Hall (525 Washington Street) or on the State Elections website  with a Massachusetts drivers license.
 Vote by Mail 
The last day to request a Vote by Mail ballot is Tuesday, October 27. The Town Clerk's Office recommends requesting ballots earlier to allow for mailing time. 
 Vote by Mail ballots must be USPS postmarked by November 3 OR delivered to the ballot drop box or the Town Clerk's Office at Town Hall (525 Washington Street) no later than 8 p.m. on Tuesday, November 3.  Vote by Mail ballots may NOT be dropped off at polling locations.
 On Election Day, November 3, voting locations will be open for in-person voting from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. 
 Precincts A & C: Upham Elementary School, 35 Wynnewood Road
 Precinct B: Sprague Elementary School, 401 School Street
 Precincts D & E: Warren Building, 90 Washington Street
 Precincts F & G: Shipley Center, Dana Hall School, 142 Grove Street
 Precinct H: Tolles Parsons Center, Council on Aging, 500 Washington Street
